what_it_states: Same scalar problem and results as arXiv 1212.1186v3 in journal form, with the added qualifier 'within the classes of mechanisms oblivious of the database and the queries beyond the global sensitivity': single real-valued query, pure epsilon-DP, sensitivity Delta, minimax expected cost for symmetric nondecreasing L with Property 2. Theorem 1 / Corollary 2 (staircase optimal), Theorem 3 (output-independence within piecewise-constant periodic families; technical condition conjectured removable), Theorem 4 (inf over all epsilon-DP laws equals inf over the staircase family; Appendix B eight-step proof), Theorem 5 (|x| cost: gamma* = 1/(1+e^{epsilon/2})), Theorem 7 (x^2 cost: gamma* real root of a cubic; minimum power formula), Corollaries 6/8 asymptotics, Theorem 9 / Corollary 10 (moment costs), heuristic gamma, discrete Theorems 11-13, abstract staircase Theorem 14 (2 epsilon-DP). Section I-D7 remark: per-coordinate staircase for d linear queries gives an upper bound. Conclusion: notes the staircase extension to the multidimensional setting in its reference [53] (Geng-Kairouz-Oh-Viswanath JSTSP 2015, the inventory's P_G15) and approximate DP in [54]. Acknowledgment: the same class of staircase mechanisms appeared in Soria-Comas/Domingo-Ferrer slides [55] under a different optimization framework; related journal paper [56].
what_it_does_not_state: No planar or l1-diamond statement; no all-law squared-Euclidean MSE value or selector in dimension two; no mixed-cost all-law bound E||Z||_2^2 >= (2/3) inf E||Z||_1^2; no rounded-core selector. Its multidimensional content is a pointer to another inventory source plus a non-optimal upper-bound remark.
